claim: The recovery-lineage concurrency invariants were verified against a real PostgreSQL server with genuinely independent connections. This is not a claim about concurrency elsewhere in the system, and not a claim about model quality, profitability, or readiness for real-money use.

defects_this_gate_found.why_sqlite_missed_it: SQLite does not enforce VARCHAR length

defects_this_gate_found.postgres_error: none - a wrong count, not an exception
defects_this_gate_found.why_sqlite_missed_it: the threads happened to serialise on Windows; the race is real on both backends and surfaced on Linux CI as a count of 2 where the invariant is 1

execution.fallback_to_sqlite: impossible: pgconftest.require_pg_url raises when FDE_DATABASE_URL is absent or not a PostgreSQL URL, rather than defaulting
execution.independence_method: pg_backend_pid() compared between two concurrently open sessions; the suite fails if they match
execution.isolation_between_tests: one PostgreSQL schema per test via schema_translate_map, created and dropped around each case
execution.race_synchronisation: threading.Barrier(n) released simultaneously, so contention is repeatable rather than dependent on scheduling luck

locking_strategy.recovery_open: recovery keys are derived, not random, so two workers compute the same key and the second insert loses on the same unique index
locking_strategy.slot_claim: UNIQUE index on scheduled_job_runs.idempotency_key; the insert is the lock
locking_strategy.startup_reconciliation: UPDATE ... WHERE id = :id AND job_outcome = 'RUNNING'; rowcount is the ownership signal
locking_strategy.summary: every mutual-exclusion point is a single atomic statement whose outcome the loser can observe

scope_limits: Covers recovery-lineage races only, as enumerated under tests.groups.
Not a general statement about concurrency elsewhere in the system.
Not a statement about model quality, profitability, predictive superiority, production approval, or readiness for real-money use.

groups.name: TestBackendIsReallyPostgres
groups.proves: the dialect is postgresql, the module constructs no sqlite URL, and two sessions hold two different backend PIDs

groups.name: TestInitialRunRace
groups.proves: four workers claiming the same slot produce exactly one finished run and one set of domain effects; the losers receive a typed skip

groups.name: TestRecoveryRace
groups.proves: four workers recovering the same interrupted slot produce exactly one recovery branch at sequence 1, with a monotonic gap-free sequence, one root, and no duplicated domain effects

groups.name: TestAdministrativeRecoveryRace
groups.proves: concurrent administrative overrides do not stack: at most one takes effect, and it carries operator and reason

groups.name: TestInitialVersusRecoveryRace
groups.proves: ordinary recovery racing an administrative override yields exactly one active successor under one root
